title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening page of a 98-page set of notes (Dec. 1981 – Jan. 1982) on the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a stratified space. The aim is to replace a stratified space X, with strata indexed by a poset I, by a combinatorial system of manifolds with boundary (really with corners) and fibrations. X should then be recoverable by collapsing.

The three-strata model (i<j<k, where i<j means Σ_i lies in the closure of Σ_j and is deeper):
- Σ_i, Σ_j, Σ_k are the 'unfolded strata' (strates déployées). Each is the stratum with an open tubular neighbourhood of the deeper strata removed, so it is a compact manifold with boundary.
- Σ_ij is the 'tube de raccord' (gluing tube). It is the part of ∂Σ_j lying over Σ_i. It fibres over Σ_i with fibre F_ij, the link of stratum i in stratum j. Σ_i is the 'âme' (soul) of the tube; Σ_j is the ambient unfolded stratum.
- Σ_ijk is the 'jonction'. It sits in the corner of Σ_k where the tubes from i and from j meet.
- Hooked arrows are boundary inclusions ('bordantes'). Plain arrows are proper fibrations (in the equisingular case).
- The two squares are cartesian:
  - Σ_ijk = Σ_ij ×_{Σ_j} Σ_jk, i.e. the restriction of the tube Σ_jk→Σ_j to the boundary piece Σ_ij ⊂ ∂Σ_j.
  - Σ_ijk = Σ_ik ∩ Σ_jk inside ∂Σ_k, an intersection of two boundary faces, i.e. a corner.
- Fibrewise, F_ijk (a boundary piece of F_ik) is a bundle over F_ij with fibre F_jk: the unfolded junction fibre.

The general rule is stated for flags α=(i_0<...<i_n) of I, with Σ_α ⊂ Σ_{i_n}.
- (a) Σ_α is a manifold with boundary/corners. Its boundary is the union of the Σ_{α'} with α'⊃α and α cofinal in α' (same maximum). It suffices to take α'=α∪{j} with j inserted in any gap below i_n, i.e. j ∈ I_{<i_0} ⊔ I_{i_0<·<i_1} ⊔ ... ⊔ I_{i_{n-1}<·<i_n}.
- (b) For β=(i_0,...,i_p) an initial segment of α, Σ_α→Σ_β is a fibration with compact fibres that are manifolds with boundary. The fibrewise boundary is the union of the Σ_{α'} with α⊂α', α cofinal in α' and β an initial segment of α'. Equivalently, take α∪{j} with j inserted in a gap after i_p.

Thus the unfolded object is a functor on the category of flags (barycentric subdivision of I) with two kinds of maps:
- passage to an initial segment, which gives proper fibrations;
- passage to a cofinal subflag, which gives face inclusions.

This is exactly the structure later called a manifold with fibred corners / resolution of a Thom–Mather stratified space. The next page starts the point-set foundations: the specialization preorder, the Alexandrov topology on a poset, stratifications as continuous maps X→I, and 'stratification fidèle'.
errors: In the 'Cas non singulier' item b) the fibration is written Σ_ik → Σ_k. By the diagram, the 'âme' convention and the general rule (b) (fibrations go to initial segments), it should be Σ_ik → Σ_i, whose fibres F_ik have boundary the union of the F_ijk (i<j<k). Σ_ik → Σ_k is a boundary inclusion. This is either a slip by Grothendieck or a misreading.

'Variété à bord' is used loosely. As soon as there are three or more strata, Σ_k has corners: the faces Σ_ik and Σ_jk meet along Σ_ijk. So the correct notion is manifold with corners, with fibred corner structure. The page states the boundary is a 'réunion' of the faces but does not mention that they intersect in corners.
The structure is only asserted (equisingular case, existence of tubes/control data assumed); no proof or existence statement for the unfolding is given on this page.

ideas.what: Unfolding a stratified space into unfolded strata (compact manifolds with boundary/corners) joined by gluing tubes fibred over deeper strata, with link fibres F_ij and junctions Σ_ijk, in cartesian squares
ideas.modern_name: Resolution / unfolding of Thom–Mather stratified spaces; manifolds with fibred corners; 'unzipping'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969) and Mather (1970) for control data; Verona (Stratified Mappings, LNM 1102, 1984) for resolution; Brasselet–Hector–Saralegi (1992) for unfoldings; Melrose and Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza (2012) for fibred corners; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017) for unzipping of conically smooth spaces
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6, sketches the 'dévissage' of tame stratified structures into a system of manifolds with boundary and tubes indexed by flags. The details are only on such manuscripts.

ideas.what: Indexing of the unfolded pieces Σ_α by flags α of the stratum poset. Initial-segment maps are proper fibrations; cofinal-subflag maps are face inclusions. Generating faces are obtained by inserting one index into a gap.
ideas.modern_name: Functor on the barycentric subdivision sd(P) (flag category); compare 'décollages' (Haine; Barwick–Glasman–Haine) and AFT's description via links
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017); Haine (2018) and Barwick–Glasman–Haine (Exodromy) for the sd(P) homotopical version
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse §5 (flags of strata); not in explicit form.

ideas.what: Iterated link structure: F_ijk is a bundle over F_ij with fibre F_jk (the link of i in k contains a boundary piece fibred by links)
ideas.modern_name: Iterated (recursive) links; fibred boundary of links in conically stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mather, Goresky (1978), Siebenmann (1972), Quinn (1988, homotopy links)

missed.claim: Grothendieck organizes the unfolded stratified space as a diagram indexed by flags of the stratum poset, with two classes of morphisms (initial segment → fibration, cofinal subflag → boundary inclusion). This is essentially the sd(P)-indexed description used three decades later. It amounts to an early combinatorial form of the AFT unzipping and of the décollage picture of stratified homotopy theory, and as far as I know it is not credited to him there.
missed.quote: Σ_{i_0 ··· i_n} = Σ_α → Σ_{i_0 ··· i_p} = Σ_β est fibrant, à fibres des variétés à bord compactes, le fibré des bords est réunion des Σ_α' avec α' ⊃ α, α cofinal dans α', β segment initial de α'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The flag-indexed two-variance structure is the precise shape of Ayala–Francis–Tanaka's unzipping and of Barwick–Glasman–Haine's décollages. Grothendieck's 98 pages may contain a reconstruction (collapse) theorem or equivalence statement predating these; historians of stratified homotopy theory would want to credit it.

missed.claim: The page posits (in the equisingular case) that every stratified space has such a 'déploiement'. The implied equivalence between tame stratified spaces and flag-indexed systems of manifolds with corners plus fibrations (the 'dévissage' theorem announced in the Esquisse) is not proved here.
missed.quote: les flèches → sont des fibrations (propres) (cas équisingulier)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only partial versions exist (Verona, ALMP for Thom–Mather spaces, AFT for conically smooth spaces). A clean equivalence in the o-minimal/'tame' setting Grothendieck envisaged remains not fully standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the now-familiar resolution into manifolds with fibred corners. It is known from Thom–Mather/Verona/ALMP/AFT and sketched by Grothendieck himself in the Esquisse. The explicit flag-indexed rules (cofinal versus initial segment, generating faces by gap insertion) are a neat, early, uncredited combinatorial formulation anticipating sd(P)-based descriptions, but the page is not surprising to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The arrows between Σ_ik and Σ_ijk, and between Σ_k and Σ_jk, are drawn double-headed in the image, not as Σ_ijk → Σ_ik and Σ_jk → Σ_k. By the rules on the page they should be boundary inclusions Σ_ijk ↪ Σ_ik and Σ_jk ↪ Σ_k.
Item 'Cas non singulier b)': the image indeed reads 'Σ_ik → Σ_k fibrations compactes'. Mathematically this should be Σ_ik → Σ_i.
Diagram fibre labels read (F_ik), (F_ij), (F_jk) on the arrows Σ_ik→Σ_i, Σ_ij→Σ_i, Σ_jk→Σ_j respectively.
